Subject: Re: Performance run results (ClearBank) — summary + artifacts

All — completed the full run this morning. Putting a concise summary here and dropping the CSV artifact (concurrency_results_20260625.csv) into the Drive link. Full raw traces are in the Drive folder. Highlights:

Summary results (steady-state = 1.2k QPS sustained; bursts = 2.5k for 20s windows):
- Steady-state (1.2k):
  - p50 latency: 110ms
  - p95 latency: 410ms
  - TTFT median: 120ms
  - KV cache hitrate: 62% (prefix caching enabled)
  - Observed token throughput: 1.35M tokens/min across the pool
- Burst windows (2.5k spikes):
  - Immediate effect: average queue length grew to ~180 requests, queue latency added ~220ms p95 for queued requests
  - Short-lived tail spikes: occasional p99 > 6s when queue depth peaked and upstream auth had transient errors
  - Request failures: <0.2% (timeouts), retriable at client side

Operational notes & recommendations:
1) Rate-limit tuning — set soft QPS guard at 1.35k and hard cap at 2.2k for the route. This reduces queue growth and keeps p95 under 500ms in our runs.
2) Client backoff + jitter — recommend conservative backoff for 429s with jitter to smooth bursts.
3) Enable aggressive prefix caching for known payment templates (improved TTFT & reduced compute).
4) Canary plan — run a 24h canary with 10% traffic before full Dedicated reservation. If we see <0.5% errors and p95 < 450ms, greenlight.
5) Fallback policy — configure automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model for >2k load to avoid long tail spikes.

Attachments: concurrency_results_20260625.csv (text/csv) — includes per-second QPS, queue_depth, p50/p95/p99, TTFT buckets, and node-level CPU/GPU usage.

I'll put a short annotated results file in the Drive and tag the MAP.

—Marcus
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
